rationale.consistency: Follows surrounding style; keeps trimPathPrefix API, reuses url.PathUnescape/EqualFold idioms, removes now-dead reverse helper.
rationale.edge_cases: Handles decoded/escaped patterns, case-folded hex, non-match; but split loop can start inside an escape (path /a%2Fc, suffix Fc yields /a%2), producing a broken raw path.
rationale.scope: Targeted change plus a justified extraction of the shared matcher; no unrelated edits, dead reverse() removed.
rationale.readability: Names are clear, but the doc comment is copy-pasted verbatim onto both pathPrefixMatchLen and trimPathPrefix, and the brute-force scan lacks a note on why it is safe/cheap.
rationale.robustness: No panics (slice bounds safe); however mid-escape false positives can emit an invalid %-sequence into RawPath. O(n*m) scan per request is acceptable for short paths.
rationale.maintainability: Single shared matcher avoids logic duplication, but the try-every-offset approach hides the escape-boundary flaw and is less direct than a reverse lock-step walk.
